scenes.title: The Enthymeme Before a Crowd
scenes.summary: The enthymeme should neither reason from far off nor state the obvious, which is why the uneducated persuade crowds better than the educated; it should start from what the judges accept, and from what holds for the most part as well as from necessities.

scenes.title: Knowing the Facts
scenes.summary: One must know the facts of the subject: the Athenians' power, revenues and wars; their victories at Salamis and Marathon, and their wrongs to Aegina and Potidaea; and those proper to it, as Achilles killed Hector and Cycnus, not those common to many.

scenes.title: Demonstrative and Refutative Enthymemes
scenes.summary: The elements, or topics, of enthymemes follow. Enthymemes are demonstrative or refutative; the special topics have been given, so the general ones remain, with the apparent enthymemes, solutions and objections.
